unfavorable trials, invalid measurements and unfinished investigations. It is a
reference archive, not a ranking of incompatible experiments. Individual entries
retain the registry's original status and decision, which can differ from a
later interpretation. A failed metric, a failed execution and a measurement
correction are distinct events.

Entries are grouped by design topic for navigation. They are not pooled effects:
different datasets, prompts, source permissions and code revisions remain separate.
A reference to another run is not automatically a correction or an invalidation.
An explicit correction entry and the original record must be read together.

The fields below are bounded extracts from versioned registry rows, readable
summaries and machine records. Truncation and absent metadata are marked; full
records are linked. Structured floating-point values are displayed to six significant
figures in their original units; full precision remains in the machine record.
No raw conversation archive or private dataset is reproduced.
AI-assisted reviews described in historical sources are not independent human
assessment, even where the original source calls an assistant independent.

Source links resolve to repository paths on the main branch; they are not immutable
experiment snapshots and may be unavailable until local changes are published.
The distributed LaTeX and coverage index retain the exact local paths. The reported
code revision and original experiment manifests, not the hyperlink branch, govern
reproduction. Missing historical artifacts are not reconstructed.



For narrative reading, use the design-topic headings, decision and failure
explanation. The Run field is a stable lookup key, not a concept to learn.
Version suffixes identify historical configurations; they do not rank quality
or imply that a later version was adopted. Configuration and provenance fields

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} The experiment asked whether an explicit, swappable gate could stop weak vocabulary-\allowbreak{}sharing out-\allowbreak{}of-\allowbreak{}domain retrieval before generation without hiding ranking failures or refusing too many answerable questions. All candidates used the same BM25 v1 ranker (k1=1.2, b=0.75) and returned only its evidence. The pre-\allowbreak{}run prediction was that absolute score would be brittle, lexical coverage would trade abstention against paraphrases, and independent semantic agreement would provide the best balance while still risking nearby-\allowbreak{}domain and multi-\allowbreak{}evidence failures. Metrics, gates, and selection order were frozen in the experiment plan before the held-\allowbreak{}out run. The any-\allowbreak{}hit control answered all 18 vocabulary-\allowbreak{}sharing negatives. This proves that "BM25 returned something" is not an evidence-\allowbreak{}sufficiency rule. [excerpt; full source linked]\par

\textbf{Configuration / comparison:} term-\allowbreak{}overlap: role = control; version = v1; configuration.tokenizer = lowercase-\allowbreak{}alphanumeric / bm25: role = candidate; version = v1; configuration.tokenizer = lowercase-\allowbreak{}alphanumeric; configuration.k1 = 1.2; configuration.b = 0.75\par

\textbf{Results / gates (extract):} term-\allowbreak{}overlap: recall-\allowbreak{}at-\allowbreak{}1=0.75 ratio; gate=True; recall-\allowbreak{}at-\allowbreak{}5=1 ratio; gate=True; mean-\allowbreak{}reciprocal-\allowbreak{}rank=0.975 ratio; gate=True; no-\allowbreak{}evidence-\allowbreak{}accuracy=1 ratio; gate=True; mean-\allowbreak{}latency=0.038 milliseconds; gate=True; peak-\allowbreak{}memory=157012 bytes; gate=True / bm25: recall-\allowbreak{}at-\allowbreak{}1=0.8 ratio; gate=True; recall-\allowbreak{}at-\allowbreak{}5=1 ratio; gate=True; mean-\allowbreak{}reciprocal-\allowbreak{}rank=1 ratio; gate=True; no-\allowbreak{}evidence-\allowbreak{}accuracy=1 ratio; gate=True; mean-\allowbreak{}latency=0.098 milliseconds; gate=True; peak-\allowbreak{}memory=160508 bytes; gate=True\par

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} BM25 improved the fraction of all gold judgments returned at rank one by five percentage points and placed a relevant result first for every evidence-\allowbreak{}bearing question. The unique-\allowbreak{}term overlap control already performed strongly, and both rankers achieved complete Recall@5. BM25's approximately 2.6-\allowbreak{}times latency and 3.5 KB peak-\allowbreak{}memory increase are operationally negligible here because the absolute measured cost stayed below 0.1 ms and 161 KB. The corpus is too small for Recall@5 to be discriminating: five results cover more than half of its nine chunks. Recall@1 and MRR provide the more meaningful signal for this run. The result supports BM25 as the next baseline, not as a final architecture or state-\allowbreak{}of-\allowbreak{}the-\allowbreak{}art claim. [excerpt; full source linked]\par

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} Calibration contained no-\allowbreak{}evidence queries with no corpus vocabulary. It chose the unthresholded BM25 control because all five returned no hits. The unseen economics query monetary policy inflation central bank interest rate shared the generic term policy with course policy and CSP chunks. BM25 therefore returned weak matches, and RRF inherited them. This is calibration-\allowbreak{}distribution failure, not a source-\allowbreak{}permission failure. No cutoff was adjusted after inspecting the held-\allowbreak{}out result. Doing so would turn the test set into training data and overstate confidence. Refine; select no replacement. [excerpt; full source linked]\par

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} The primary question was whether contextual hybrid Qwen3 reranking, R5, improved complete course evidence over heading-\allowbreak{}aware BM25, R1, enough to justify a larger confirmatory study and provisional end-\allowbreak{}to-\allowbreak{}end integration. R0-\allowbreak{}R5 were frozen for all cases, R6 was limited to the multi-\allowbreak{}evidence slice, and O1 was an oracle ceiling. R5 versus R1 was the only primary contrast. The prediction was that R5 would add at least four complete-\allowbreak{}evidence successes without reducing no-\allowbreak{}evidence accuracy. Keep and SOTA claims were unavailable at this checkpoint. R1 remained the rollback under every outcome. The one-\allowbreak{}time ledger was created at 2026-\allowbreak{}07-\allowbreak{}23T16:39:53Z. The process completed 29 of the 59 standard R0-\allowbreak{}R5 cases. It was observed alive at 2026-\allowbreak{}07-\allowbreak{}23T21:03:46Z and absent at 2026-\allowbreak{}07-\allowbreak{}23T21:18:51Z. [excerpt; full source linked]\par

\textbf{Results / gates (extract):} All 600 graph cells were durable before gold opened, and all conditions preserved scope, citations, authority, and safe fallback. The failure was therefore not a safety collapse. It had three causes: 1. Five otherwise usable planner responses carried non-\allowbreak{}authoritative reason\_\allowbreak{}code text longer than the local contract. 2. Exact agreement with one preferred action was treated as transition validity, even when another action remained inside the professor-\allowbreak{}approved event envelope. 3. The provisional ordering used exact-\allowbreak{}action agreement but omitted the preregistered continuous policy utility; deterministic A had the best mean utility (0.7830) and lowest mean regret (0.0057). C recovered much of B's model-\allowbreak{}only degradation, but A beat C on hidden utility in 30 cases while C beat A in 11. The C+V reject-\allowbreak{}only verifier over-\allowbreak{}rejected valid moves and materially regressed C. SA8: Closure = Normalize only the non-\allowbreak{}authoritative reason string before local validation; [excerpt; full source linked]\par

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} limitations = The hidden utility oracle is synthetic and does not establish real learning improvement., The post-\allowbreak{}hoc diagnostic analysis explains Fold 003 but cannot change its metrics, gates, or decision., The successor requires fresh execution and confirmation before release selection.\par

\subsubsection*{V2 finite dialogue progression}

\phantomsection\hypertarget{trial-ccf7281a7064}{}\label{trial-ccf7281a7064}

\textbf{Run:} \path{final-profile-operational-dialogue-development-001-progression-live-001}\

\textbf{Configuration / comparison:} concurrency = 2\par

\textbf{Results / gates (extract):} The Socratic incorrect-\allowbreak{}attempt history followed a useful sequence: diagnostic question, one partial cited hint, relevant explanation, then a fresh diagnostic question for a new concept. The correct Socratic attempt received an explanation. Explanatory initial and new-\allowbreak{}concept turns gave explanations, but its correct attempt still received a generic question followed by a hint. This remains a weakness in pedagogical continuation. Two further-\allowbreak{}help proposals labelled the entire requested answer as a hint. The new conservative span-\allowbreak{}coverage check rejected both (Socratic correct and never-\allowbreak{}direct-\allowbreak{}answer histories), resulting in safe graph failures. This prevents those literal full-\allowbreak{}answer hints; it does not guarantee partial disclosure when model requirement coverage is wrong. Eight delivered turns were questions, six were answers (including two hints), and two were safe graph failures.\par

\textbf{Failure / limitation (extract):} limitations = Baseline descriptive comparison only; not randomized matched treatment effect, Profile stage interpretation and partial-\allowbreak{}disclosure semantics require content review, Source fixtures do not qualify ingestion, deployed auth or human learning, Never-\allowbreak{}answer failure safely abstained but is not useful tutoring\par
